{{nihongo|'''Usaka Shrine'''|鵜坂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
At present, the main deities are {{ill|Omodaru and Ayakashikone|ja|オモダル・アヤカシコネ|zh|面足尊與惶根尊|qid=Q11152535|lt=Omodaru-no-Kami and Ayakashikone-no-Kami}}, with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usaka-hime-hiko-no-Kami}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usaka-tsuma-hiko-no-Kami}} and {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|Q11435420|qid=Q11435420}} as associated deities.

Based on the names of the associated deities, a strong theory holds that the deity called "Usaka-no-Kami," matching the shrine's name, was originally the principal deity, and that the associated deities were elder and later deities connected to that main deity.

Because shrines in former Usaka Village were {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=consolidated}} in the {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}, the following deities were additionally enshrined:
*{{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}}・{{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke Ōkami}}
*{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Honda-wake-Ōkami}}

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, its origin was an enshrinement about 2,000 years ago by {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|Q11435420|qid=Q11435420}}, the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804|lt=Hokurikudō commander}}, in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}. It is said to have been formally established in {{ill|652|Q31104|qid=Q31104}}（{{ill|Hakuchi (era)|de|Hakuchi (Ära)|es|Hakuchi (era)|fa|هاکوچی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hakuchi|hr|Hakuchi (razdoblje)|ia|Hakuchi (era)|id|Hakuchi|ja|白雉|ko|하쿠치|ru|Хакути|sh|Hakuchi (era)|simple|Hakuchi (era)|sr|Хакучи|th|ฮากูจิ (ศักราช)|tr|Hakuchi (dönem)|uk|Хакуті|zh|白雉|zh_yue|白雉|qid=Q540118}} 2）. In the Heian period it rose to {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|fa|شینکای (رتبه الهی)|ja|神階|qid=Q11591025}}{{ill|Junior Third Rank|Q11071123|qid=Q11071123}} and was revered by the {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|Q30253177|qid=Q30253177|lt=imperial court}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as a small shrine.

In the {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} period, Usaka-dera of the {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} was built and flourished as a {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}. It declined, however, due to repeated damage during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}} and flooding from the nearby {{ill|Jinzū River|Q1156518|qid=Q1156518}}. The temple was abolished in {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} during {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}}. No temple halls survive.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} it was ranked as a {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

== Festivals ==
*New Year Festival  January 1
*National Foundation Festival  February 11
*Prayer for Good Harvest Festival  February 23
*Annual Grand Festival  April 29
*Insect-Exorcism Festival / Iemochi Akira Festival / Usaka-dera Bettō Memorial Rite  June 16
*Niinamesai  November 23

From the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} to the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, a special ritual called the Nari Festival was held. Also called the "Buttocks-Striking Festival," it was a rite said to admonish women about chastity. It derived from a courtly custom claiming that striking women's buttocks with firewood used to cook {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=nanakusa-gayu}} in the New Year would result in healthy children. As one of the "Five Great Strange Festivals of Japan," it became known nationwide, and was even composed about by {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}} and {{ill|Takarai Kikaku|Q2118326|qid=Q2118326}}. In the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was changed to a rite of striking a mare's buttocks, and around the end of {{ill|World War II|Q362|qid=Q362|lt=the Second World War}} it was discontinued.

== Facilities ==
The honden stands with the Jinzū River to its rear, with the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}} and {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} placed in front.

To the left of the haiden remain gravestones and other traces of Usaka-dera. A waka poem composed when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Etchū}}{{ill|Kokushi (official)|Q1351234|qid=Q1351234}} {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|qid=Q386308}} visited this place is carved on the "Usaka River Poem Monument."

On the approach there is a stone called "Ibo-ishi" (wart stone), believed to be efficacious for warts and hemorrhoids. For warts, one rubs the affected area; for hemorrhoids, one quietly sits on it.
